in_english.name: Ilahiyaht
in_english.meaning: Derived from Ilahiyah, meaning divine or sacred
in_english.long_meaning: Ilahiyaht is a name derived from the Arabic word 'Ilahiyah', meaning divine, sacred, or related to God. This name is used in various Muslim cultures to signify closeness to God and to reflect divine attributes. Etymologically, it connects to the root 'A-L-H', which is fundamental in Islamic theology, emphasizing the oneness and uniqueness of God.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ilahiyaht" serves as a reminder of the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and supremacy of God in all aspects of life. By acknowledging that all things originate from and belong to God, this name inherently fosters a society that values submission and obedience to the divine will, as is expressed through acts of reverence and devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Ilahiyaht" resonates with the idea of Tawhid, the Islamic doctrine of monotheism that stresses the unity of God. It is a constant reminder of the spiritual interconnectedness of all things and beings, and a call to live in accordance with the divine will. This name also represents a deep sense of humility, acknowledging that all blessings and possessions come from God, and thus, should be used in His service and for the benefit of others. Furthermore, it invites one to reflect on the transient nature of this world and the eternal consequences of actions in the hereafter. Overall, the significance of "Ilahiyaht" serves as a powerful spiritual compass in navigating life's journey towards self-improvement, devotion, and ultimately, enlightenment.
